requirements.requirement:
Status: verbindliche Arbeitsanweisung für die erste produktionsreife Implementierung
Ziel: ein sicherheitsorientiertes, dezentrales Discovery-System für öffentliche Tor Onion Services ohne Änderungen oder Neukompilierung von Tor.
Projektname: Onion Service Discovery. Dieser Name MUSS ausgeschrieben und konsistent verwendet werden. Keine Abkürzung als Produkt- oder Protokollname.

MUSS:
- Opt-in: Ein Onion Service darf nur in den öffentlichen Discovery-Index gelangen, wenn er dies explizit in seinem eigenen Discovery-Manifest erklärt.
- Zero Renewal: Nach der Erstkonfiguration darf keine periodische manuelle Registrierung erforderlich sein.
- Self-hosted Metadata: Name, Beschreibung, Kategorien, Sprachen und Discovery-Schalter stammen primär vom Onion Service selbst.
- No Central Authority: Kein einzelner Node darf für Funktion, Identität oder Suche erforderlich sein.
- Web Local Search: In der unveränderten Referenzimplementierung werden Suchbegriffe ausschließlich lokal im Browser verarbeitet. Ein bösartiger/kompromittierter Serving Node kann jedoch manipulierten Web-Code ausliefern; diese Origin-Trust-Grenze ist ausdrücklich Teil des Threat Models.
- Tor-only Network Access: Node-zu-Node- und Node-zu-Service-Kommunikation erfolgt für .onion-Ziele ausschließlich über Tor SOCKS mit Remote-Hostname-Auflösung.
- No Tor Key Access: Die Anwendung darf niemals den privaten Hidden-Service-Key von Tor lesen, kopieren, importieren oder als Anwendungsidentität verwenden.
- Separate Keys: Service Identity Key und Node Identity Key sind getrennte Ed25519-Schlüssel.
- Explicit Trust Semantics: UI darf nicht pauschal “trusted”, “safe”, “legit” oder vergleichbare Aussagen anzeigen.
- Untrusted Peers: Daten von Peers sind Hinweise/Behauptungen und werden nicht allein durch Empfang wahr.
- Direct Verification: Kritische Service-Metadaten werden soweit praktikabel direkt beim betreffenden Onion Service verifiziert.
- Privacy by Design: Keine Suchbegriffe in Logs, Node-Requests, Telemetrie oder Fehlermeldungsdiensten.
- Fail Closed: Bei Signaturfehlern, Parsing-Mehrdeutigkeiten, Onion-Mismatch, Hash-Mismatch, Key-Mismatch oder Protokollverletzungen wird ein Datensatz verworfen bzw. quarantänisiert.
- Bounded Resources: Größenlimits, Zeitlimits, Rate Limits, maximale Peerzahlen, maximale Kandidatenzahlen und Backoff sind verpflichtend.
- Secure Defaults: Publish, Mirror und Discover müssen getrennt konfigurierbar sein; riskantere Funktionen dürfen nicht unbemerkt aktiviert werden.
- No Hidden Network Side Effects: Normale Webseitenbesuche des Nutzers dürfen nicht automatisch als Discovery-Signale an Nodes gemeldet werden.
- Reproducibility: Release-Artefakte, Abhängigkeiten, SBOM und Prüfsummen müssen nachvollziehbar sein.

Ein Service-Manifest MUSS mindestens enthalten:
- protocol = "Onion Service Discovery"
- protocol_version
- onion
- service_identity_public_key
- revision
- previous_manifest_hash, außer Genesis
- publish_service
- service.name
- service.description optional, aber begrenzt
- languages
- categories
- signature

Das Manifest MUSS direkt von derselben Onion-Adresse abrufbar sein, die im Feld onion steht.
Bei Identitätsprüfung sind HTTP-Redirects auf andere Hosts/Onions verboten.
Die Onion-v3-Adresse selbst bleibt Tor-Identität; die Anwendung führt zusätzlich einen Onion Service Discovery Service Identity Key, ohne Tor-Schlüssel zu berühren.

Jeder Mirror/Discovery-Node besitzt einen separaten Ed25519 Node Identity Key.
Node-Key signiert:
- Observations
- Node-Metadaten
- ggf. Snapshot-/Merkle-Roots
Node-Key DARF NICHT Service-Metadaten umschreiben.
Ein Service und sein Node dürfen auf derselben Maschine laufen, Schlüssel bleiben getrennt.
Onion Service Discovery is not considered fully designed merely because the Protocol, PHP Node and Web Local Search Client are specified. The project additionally requires:

33. STORAGE BACKEND FREEDOM
Onion Service Discovery MUST NOT require SQLite or any particular database product.
The selected backend is an operator decision. Protocol semantics MUST remain identical across backends.

37. SOFTWARE UPDATE TRUST
Production release trust MUST NOT reduce to “GitHub says this is the latest file”.
Use a mature signed update-metadata design with rollback/freeze protection and protected root trust.

FINAL COMPLETENESS RULE
The agent must copy the normative glossary and known-limitations document into the implementation repository and keep them synchronized with behavior. Any new security claim or security-semantic term requires review against both documents.

1. RELEASE-KLASSEN
- Prototype: experimentell, keinerlei Produktionsversprechen.
- Alpha: grundlegende Interoperabilität, bekannte Lücken zulässig.
- Beta: vollständige Kernfunktionen, Security-Hardening läuft.

27. FINAL CLAIM RULE
“Production-ready” is forbidden until all original and extended gates are PASS.
“Protocol Version 1 Stable” is forbidden until formal, conformance, standards-publication and Protocol/Crypto human-review gates are PASS.
“Production Stable” additionally requires chaos, accessibility, operator experience, capacity, corpus, archaeology and ecosystem/succession gates.

28. SQLITE RUNTIME GATE
The PHP reference node MUST explicitly verify PDO SQLite availability.
Production documentation MUST NOT state or imply that SQLite support is guaranteed to exist in every PHP installation.
Missing SQLite MUST NOT block an operator who selected FilesystemStore.
init/doctor/security:check MUST verify the PDO SQLite driver explicitly and fail clearly when absent.

Normative Arbeitsgrundlage für die Referenzimplementierungen. Die Schlüsselwörter MUSS, DARF NICHT, SOLL, SOLL NICHT und KANN sind normativ zu verstehen.

4. Manifest-Grundstruktur
Version 1 MUSS logisch mindestens folgende Felder besitzen:

5. Onion-Feld

- Der direkte Verifier MUSS prüfen, dass das onion-Feld genau dem Host entspricht, gegen den die Verifikation durchgeführt wurde.

- Ein Mismatch führt zu REJECT oder QUARANTINE gemäß Ursache.
- Die Anwendung DARF NICHT versuchen, den privaten Tor-Onion-Schlüssel zu lesen.

8. Hashes
Version 1 verwendet einen dokumentierten kryptografischen Hash für Inhaltsreferenzen. Die Referenzimplementierung soll SHA-256 verwenden, sofern bis zur Implementierung kein stärker begründeter Standard gewählt und per ADR dokumentiert wird.

2. Laufzeit
Bei Implementierungsbeginn ist eine aktuell unterstützte, sichere PHP-Version zu wählen und per ADR festzuschreiben.
Pflicht-Extensions:
- sodium;
- curl;
- PDO SQLite.
Composer wird mit Lockfile verwendet.

Known-Answer-Tests sind Pflicht.
Die Signatur darf niemals über eine zufällige Standard-json_encode-Ausgabe erzeugt werden.

Keys und DB können unterschiedliche Schutz-/Backupstrategien haben.

42. STORAGE BACKEND PLUG-IN ARCHITECTURE
The PHP reference Node MUST depend on a StorageBackend interface rather than SQLite-specific repository code.
It MUST NOT store attacker-controlled strings as raw path names.

Therefore the project MUST distinguish:
A. “Reference Web Client design sends search queries nowhere.”
B. “A malicious serving Node cannot be cryptographically prevented from serving modified browser code.”

14. Large Index Strategy

39. Navigation
Opening a Service requires user action.
Reparse canonical Onion.
Construct destination internally.
No javascript:, data:, file:, custom scheme from metadata.

47. Node Branding
A Node may style surrounding page minimally but MUST NOT alter reference security-label semantics if claiming Reference Web Client conformance.
This limitation MUST be in Known Limitations and threat model.

40. Production Acceptance
Operations gelten als fertig, wenn ein unabhängiger Clean-Room-Test Installation, Upgrade, Backup, Restore, Scheduler, Health und Rollback praktisch nachweisen kann und alle Runbooks als ausführbar bewertet wurden.

2. PRIORITÄT DER QUELLEN
Bei Konflikten:
A. Security-Invarianten und explizite MUST/MUSS-Regeln.
B. Protocol Specification.
C. Master Execution Brief.
D. Component Specifications.
E. Architecture.
F. Beispiele/Illustrationen.

8. SECURITY INVARIANTS ALS CODE
Erzeuge eine Datei docs/security/invariants.md und testbare IDs:
SEC-INV-001 Private Tor key never read by application.
SEC-INV-002 Direct manifest host equals manifest onion.
SEC-INV-003 Peer assertion never becomes direct observation without direct verification.
SEC-INV-004 Lower revision never replaces higher valid revision.
SEC-INV-005 Equal revision/different hash is fork.
SEC-INV-006 Key change requires valid rotation proof.

SEC-INV-008 Search query never leaves client.

SEC-INV-010 Resource usage bounded.
Weitere Invarianten aus Threat Model ergänzen.

# 10 - Required Engineering Review and Release Templates

## Human Review
Required:
Reviewer:
Status:

Status
Normative external-reference baseline, verified 11 October 2026. This document does not freeze third-party standards forever. The coding agent MUST re-check all time-sensitive dependencies and platform behavior at implementation start, at protocol freeze, and before every production release.

1. Purpose
Onion Service Discovery intentionally relies on established standards and official platform behavior instead of inventing equivalents. This document records which external specifications are authoritative, which facts are stable protocol assumptions, and which facts are time-sensitive and MUST be refreshed.

Implementation consequence:
The PHP transport adapter MUST pass the Onion hostname through the Tor SOCKS connection rather than resolving it locally.
It MUST NOT use a local DNS lookup as fallback.
It MUST NOT fall back to a direct TCP connection if Tor is unavailable.
Transport error mapping SHOULD preserve useful Onion-service failure classes internally when available without making application correctness depend on implementation-specific extended codes.

This decision requires ADR and integration tests.
Do not invent a custom Tor-control dependency merely to obtain isolation if ordinary SOCKS semantics satisfy the defined threat model.

requirements.section: 7. Tor Browser Fingerprinting and Web Privacy Model
requirements.requirement:
New trust boundary:
the Node that serves the Web Client can modify that executable code. The project MUST document this and MUST NOT claim unconditional query secrecy against the serving origin.

requirements.section: 8. Tor Browser Web Platform Behavior — REFRESH
requirements.requirement:
The Web Local Search client MUST work without assuming durable browser storage.
If JavaScript is unavailable, the optional server-search fallback MUST remain usable without requiring users to lower Tor Browser security settings.

Project policy:
- Preferred initial production target: PHP 8.5 unless deployment constraints justify another supported branch.
- Do not choose a version already outside active security support for a new production baseline.
- CI SHOULD test at least the production minimum and latest supported compatible branch.
- Support matrix MUST contain explicit EOL dates.
- Release gate fails if a targeted runtime has reached end of security support without a migration plan.

Protocol requirement:
Before Protocol v1 freeze, produce cross-language known-answer vectors that prove PHP and TypeScript emit identical canonical bytes.
The project MUST NOT rely on language-default object iteration order or ordinary json_encode/JSON.stringify output as an implicit signature format.
Logging design MUST balance security detection with privacy and minimization.

SBOM generation MUST be automated and attached/referenced in release evidence.
SBOM is not itself a vulnerability scan.

17. Semantic Versioning
Software versioning may use Semantic Versioning if confirmed by ADR.
Protocol versioning is separate and stricter.
A software release may change without changing Protocol v1.
A breaking wire-semantic change requires a new protocol version regardless of software SemVer.

18. RFC 3339 / Time
If protocol timestamps are used, UTC RFC 3339-compatible representation SHOULD be used after ADR confirmation.
Identity ordering MUST NOT rely on wall-clock time where revision/hash-chain semantics provide stronger ordering.
Clock skew MUST NOT repair cryptographic conflict.

19. Unicode
Unicode handling must be version-aware and deterministic where security decisions depend on it.
The protocol MUST NOT sign a transformed display string unless that transformation is explicitly part of the canonical data model.
Display-layer confusable analysis is advisory and separate from cryptographic identity.

20. SQLite
SQLite is the reference node datastore, not a wire-level requirement.
The agent MUST pin/test a minimum SQLite capability set through the PHP runtime.
Foreign keys, transactions, integrity checks, locking behavior, and backup procedure require explicit tests.
Do not rely on unspecified filesystem semantics.

29. Evidence
At each production release, release evidence MUST record the versions actually used:
PHP
Composer
SQLite
Tor tested versions
Tor Browser/Firefox basis
Node/TypeScript toolchain
canonicalization implementation
crypto provider
SBOM format
CI/provenance format
OWASP/verification baseline

RFC 8615 defines the /.well-known/ URI path prefix and the associated registration framework.
Onion Service Discovery uses a Well-Known Manifest path and MUST maintain an IANA-registration readiness plan.
Before any registration request, refresh the current IANA registry and registration procedure.

Verified planning baseline:
JSON Schema Draft 2020-12 is the current published specification baseline.
Protocol v1 schemas MUST explicitly declare the dialect, use stable $id values, define unknown-field semantics, and be validated by multiple implementations where practical.

Verified planning baseline:
WCAG 2.2 is a W3C Recommendation. It is also recognized as ISO/IEC 40500:2025.
Reference-client UI and public human-facing documentation target applicable WCAG 2.2 Level AA requirements.
A project claim of conformance requires actual assessment evidence; no external certification is implied.

35. FORMAL METHODS
Formal verification tooling is not an Internet standard dependency, but the project requires an explicit reproducible formal state model for critical Protocol state semantics.
Tool/version is recorded in release evidence.

36. STANDARDS SUBMISSION CLAIM RULE
The project may prepare:
IANA registration drafts
RFC-style publications
standards-body discussion material
but MUST NOT call Onion Service Discovery an IETF standard, RFC, IANA-approved protocol or Tor Project standard until the corresponding external process actually produces that status.
.

Status
Normative Protocol v1 companion. These values are deliberately finite. Implementations MAY impose stricter local work budgets, but MUST NOT silently accept values outside the Protocol v1 wire limits and then reinterpret them differently.
A parser MUST reject duplicate keys before semantic processing.

2. Numeric Interoperability
JSON integer values used in Protocol v1 MUST remain exactly representable by JavaScript Number:
minimum where applicable: 0
maximum: 9,007,199,254,740,991 (2^53 - 1)
Implementations MUST reject fractional, negative, NaN-like, stringified-number or out-of-range values where an integer is specified.

Stored canonical form is lowercase ASCII hostname including ".onion".
Protocol fields MUST NOT contain scheme, path, port, credentials or whitespace when the schema says OnionAddress.

Decoded length MUST equal 32 bytes.
Only URL-safe Base64 alphabet.
No padding.
Canonical encoder required.

Decoded signature length MUST equal 64 bytes.
Non-canonical encodings rejected.

Protocol signatures MUST use the canonical text exactly.
Sub-second precision is not used in Protocol v1.
Timestamps are evidence/context, not identity ordering.

8. Document Byte Limits
Limits apply to received body bytes before decompression or, if compression is later specified, both compressed and decompressed limits MUST exist.
Any expansion of these protocol limits requires Protocol Change Proposal and resource-impact tests.

9. JSON Structural Limits
Maximum nesting depth: 16.
Maximum object members at any one object: 128.
Maximum array elements unless a field has a stricter limit: 256.
Maximum JSON string length unless stricter: 4096 Unicode scalar values.
Parser MUST enforce a total byte cap in addition to structural caps.

10. Service Name
Required if publish_service=true.
Length: 1..128 Unicode scalar values.
Leading/trailing whitespace normalization policy must be deterministic.
Control characters prohibited except no embedded line control is necessary; Protocol v1 SHOULD reject C0/C1 control characters.
Bidirectional formatting/control characters are not used to establish identity; client SHOULD warn or display safely.
HTML is not interpreted.

15. Clearnet Links
Maximum: 8.
HTTPS only in Protocol v1 if enabled.
No credentials.
Maximum URL length: 2048 bytes.
No automatic fetch unless separate proof policy enables it.
Clearnet proof processing MUST have a separate outbound-policy and threat-model path.

18. Software Metadata
Implementation name: max 64 ASCII/UTF-8 safe display chars.
Implementation version: max 64.
These fields are informational and MUST NOT participate in service trust.

Important:
Liveness and identity are orthogonal internally even if a convenience aggregate status exists.
A Service can have valid identity continuity while temporarily unreachable.
A Fork is an identity/history conflict and MUST NOT be cleared merely because one branch responds faster.

27. Direct Verification Redirect Policy
For /.well-known/onion-service-discovery.json:
- maximum redirects: 0 for identity-binding verification.
If future protocol explicitly supports same-host redirects, it requires Protocol Change Proposal; current v1 does not.

28. Compression
Protocol v1 baseline SHOULD serve uncompressed or ordinary HTTP content coding only if both implementations safely enforce decompressed limits.
A malicious compressed response MUST NOT bypass maximum expanded size.
If robust expanded-limit enforcement is not implemented, disable compressed responses for verification paths.

29. Ordering
Arrays whose ordering has no semantic meaning MUST have a defined signing/canonicalization rule.
Preferred Protocol v1 approach:
- semantic arrays that are sets are required to be lexicographically sorted in their canonical manifest form and contain no duplicates;
- sequence/history arrays where order matters preserve order.

31. Null vs Absent
Unless a schema explicitly states otherwise:
Optional field absent is canonical.
Explicit null is rejected.
Genesis previous_manifest_hash is the one intentional nullable field if Protocol v1 schema retains that design; alternatively a genesis-specific absent rule may be chosen before freeze. The agent MUST freeze exactly one representation and vector-test it.

33. Duplicate Semantic Values
languages, categories, peers, related_onion_services and capabilities MUST NOT contain duplicates after canonical comparison.
Reject signed input with duplicates rather than silently rewriting before verification.

35. Ports
Protocol v1 direct Service Manifest verification uses the service’s configured standard HTTP endpoint as defined by implementation/operator mapping; network-sourced candidates MUST NOT choose arbitrary ports.
If alternate public ports are to become protocol metadata, a later explicit specification is required.

36. Work Budgets
Protocol limits are not sufficient against DoS.
Reference node MUST also define local:
max new candidates accepted per peer per interval
max verification attempts per maintenance run
max concurrent Tor requests
max bytes per peer sync run
max records applied per transaction
max learned peers retained
max database growth warning/hard thresholds

37. Quarantine Retention
Security-conflict evidence such as forks SHOULD remain long enough for diagnosis and MUST NOT be discarded merely to make current state look clean.
Retention schedule is operator policy but must have a disk budget.

38. Deterministic Sorting for Exports
Snapshot/chunk exports MUST sort records using an explicit binary/text key, such as canonical Onion hostname followed by Service Identity key and revision.
Locale-aware sorting is forbidden.

40. Protocol Limit Registry Artifact
The coding agent MUST create:
protocol/limits.json
and generate or verify JSON Schemas/tests against the same constants where practical.
Do not maintain multiple manually divergent copies.

Status
Normative security companion for Protocol v1. Cryptographic construction MUST be independently reviewed before Protocol v1 freeze.
B and C MUST be distinct keypairs even if same server/operator.

6. Domain Separation
Each record type MUST use a distinct ASCII domain prefix.

The exact strings are normative and MUST be included in test vectors.
A signature valid for one record class MUST NOT validate as another class.

Full public key remains authoritative.
Fingerprint presentation MUST be deterministic and version-independent.
If a short fingerprint is displayed, UI must allow full fingerprint/key access.

Required authorization:
old key signature.

Observation MUST NOT sign arbitrary raw HTTP body.
It references validated manifest hash.
PHP and TypeScript vectors MUST compare exact UTF-8 bytes.

40. Crypto Test Vectors
Required:
fixed seed/private/public pair for tests only
canonical manifest payload
domain-prefixed message bytes in hex
signature
hash
rotation payload/signatures
migration payload/signature
node descriptor signature
observation signature
invalid bit-flipped signatures
wrong-domain verification cases

8. State Identifier
A state identifier MUST be content-derived or otherwise unambiguous.
Preferred:
root hash of deterministic index export plus generation metadata.
It MUST distinguish signed source data from local observation metadata.

16. Chunk Format
Protocol v1 MUST freeze one:
A. canonical JSON object/array with deterministic ordering; or
B. newline-delimited canonical JSON records.

24. CORS
Reference Web Local Search uses same-origin Node endpoints by default, so broad CORS is unnecessary. Any future cross-origin browser fetch requires ADR and privacy/security review.
API should not grant credentialed wildcard access.
No cookies are needed for standard read sync.

If Protocol v1 includes a public one-time announcement mechanism, prefer a separate carefully bounded endpoint and threat model.
It MUST NOT be necessary for synchronization.
It MUST NOT accept arbitrary URL.
It accepts only canonical OnionAddress plus possibly proof-of-work/challenge fields if later approved.
Rate-limit aggressively.
This feature may be omitted from v1 production and handled manually/out-of-band without harming core protocol.

46. API Schema Files
Coding agent MUST produce JSON Schemas/OpenAPI for:
node response
state
peers
service
changes

chunk format
error envelope

49. Backward Compatibility
Within Protocol v1:
server MAY add HTTP headers.

50. Acceptance
Abuse resistance passes only when automated stress tests demonstrate bounded:
memory
disk
CPU/work
network attempts
queue sizes
and valid existing search/index operation degrades gracefully under attack.

5. Network Update Independence
Index update scheduling MUST NOT be triggered synchronously by query text.
A user searching “X” should not cause a node fetch containing, identifying or predictably encoding “X”.
Updates use startup/periodic/manual generic triggers.

6. Browser Navigation
When user explicitly opens an Onion result, normal Tor Browser navigation occurs outside the Discovery protocol’s search-index request flow.
Reference client MUST NOT send a “clicked result” event to Discovery Nodes.

9. Node Request Metadata
A node necessarily receives transport-level connection traffic through Tor, but application design SHOULD avoid creating additional identifiers:
no user account
no cookie
no install UUID
no auth token for public reads
no query fingerprint
no persistent client-specific header unless protocol requires.

10. User-Agent Policy
Reference client/node sync User-Agent behavior requires privacy review.
Prefer generic project/version or minimal standard header if required for interoperability.
Do not generate per-installation variations.

search query history
favorites
pins unless user explicitly selects identity diagnostic
private keys
full production config secrets
raw browser history

28. IP/Clearnet Prohibition
Reference client does not use direct clearnet fallback for Discovery when Onion nodes fail.
A fallback would materially alter privacy and requires new architecture/human approval.

publish_service=false or manifest removal:
does not retroactively erase cryptographic observations from all decentralized nodes.
UI/search policy:

Documentation MUST explain decentralized persistence limits.

Project MUST NOT promise global deletion from independent decentralized nodes.
It can provide reference-node retention/withdrawal behavior and local deletion controls.
Legal obligations depend on operator jurisdiction and require legal review outside this technical spec.
Tests MUST cover all.

recommendations based on behavior
requires Privacy ADR and human review.

with:

tests.

Privacy is PASS only if architecture and automated instrumentation prove:
no query exfiltration

1. Core Decision
Onion Service Discovery MUST NOT require a specific database product.

2. Required Reference Backends
The reference implementation SHOULD provide at minimum:
- FilesystemStore — no SQL/database server required;
- SQLiteStore — simple embedded SQL backend.

3. No Hidden Database Dependency
Core Protocol logic MUST NOT import PDO, SQLite, PostgreSQL or MySQL-specific APIs directly.

4. StorageBackend Contract
The abstraction MUST expose behavior, not SQL concepts.
A sync cursor MUST NOT advance unless the corresponding state mutation is durably committed.
It MUST NOT be a loose collection of ad-hoc JSON files.

17. Filesystem Scale Limit
FilesystemStore MUST publish a tested supported scale.

It MUST NOT expose private keys by default.

27. Backend Conformance Suite
Every storage adapter MUST pass the same black-box StorageBackend conformance tests.
On restart, invariants MUST hold.

29. No Semantic Backend Drift
Given the same validated event stream and configuration, all conformant backends MUST derive the same Protocol-relevant current state.

41. Removal of SQLite Global Requirement
Any existing requirement stating that Onion Service Discovery as a whole requires SQLite is superseded.
This requires no extension and works with ordinary browser navigation.

9. Data-Only Discovery Node Interface
Discovery Nodes MUST NOT return executable JavaScript/HTML inside protocol data.

10. Cross-Origin Data Fetch
If Client Host and Discovery Nodes use different Onion origins, browser access requires an explicit cross-origin design.
Exact Tor Browser privacy behavior for cross-origin requests MUST be revalidated against current supported versions before freeze.
The proxy MUST remain query-independent.

28. Malicious Node Ranking
Data Nodes MUST NOT send executable ranking logic.
UI MUST NOT imply stronger isolation than exists.
Exact parameters MUST be benchmarked and frozen in the key-file format specification before release.

10. Unattended Restart Reality
If the same compromised host can automatically retrieve both ciphertext and KEK, encryption at rest does not protect against a fully compromised running host.
Documentation MUST state this.

13. Privilege Separation
Web request handling MUST NOT need Service Identity private key in the preferred profile.
Sync/discovery workers MUST NOT need Service Identity private key.
Only signing workflow accesses it.

2. Separation

10. Release Provenance

13. Rollback

Older vulnerable release MUST NOT be accepted as current merely because correctly signed historically.

17. Release Tag Immutability
Never replace artifact bytes under same version/tag.
Correction requires new release version.

19. No Auto-Execute
Onion Service Discovery MUST NOT download and automatically execute unverified code.
Operator-controlled update remains default unless a separately reviewed updater exists.
Exact format requires new Protocol proposal and vectors.
The AI agent MUST NOT fake these approvals.
